title: Active Product Knowledge lock preserves version identity while Response Semantics remains fail-closed
research_question: How does Product consume reviewed Knowledge without allowing semantic representation or an updated file to silently authorize runtime behavior?
before_state: A source-reviewed semantic record or a newly available Knowledge artifact could be mistaken for a compiled and executable Product rule.
result: The active Product Knowledge lock pins KIB-PRODUCT-20261021-V0_3 with artifact and semantic digests, records its source commit, disables auto-refresh, and defines rollback to a previous validated bundle. Response Semantics v0.2/v0.3 separately reports 8/8 pilot records preserved as semantic-only, 0/8 runtime effects authorized, and for Career 12 condition-IR-ready rows pending Product compilation with 14 local-ready rows still not condition-IR-ready; compilation and execution unlock remain zero.
key_insights: The active lock is a versioned Product dependency, not a promise that every downstream component is fully validated.
Response semantic expressibility is distinct from permission to cause runtime effects.
The current readiness census is explicit about zero compiled conditions and zero execution unlocks.

A promotion acceptance document still labels its validation pending while the current lock says KIB v0.3 is active; this is a documentation/status discrepancy to preserve and reconcile, not silently resolve.
negative_findings: No Response Compiler, ResponseProfile tau, M0 manifestation, empirical probability or predictive validity is claimed by the cited promotion note.
A semantic-only record or synthetic positive-path fixture does not authorize real runtime effects.

boundaries.source_status: Explicit in the accepted lock and adapter/readiness artifacts; one acceptance note has a stale/pending status that remains visible.
boundaries.implementation_status: Version lock is active; semantic adapter/readiness exists; compiler and runtime effects remain unauthorized in the cited readiness baseline.
